domain: ambient air quality monitoring / day-ahead pollutant exceedance
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support (rejected before construction): for an Automatic Urban and Rural Network (AURN) monitoring station, will the next-day (D+1) 24-hour mean PM2.5 concentration exceed the relevant UK air-quality objective threshold, given only that station's own hourly history through the end of day D?
prediction_time: Would be end of day D (station-day grain). Not evidenced further: the task is rejected on shape, which is independent of the instant.
target_definition: Station-day exceedance of a UK air-quality objective for a pollutant carried by the AURN (PM2.5 annual/daily objectives, ozone, NO2). Not built.

The reject below does not depend on the licence.

jurisdiction.publisher: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), UK AIR / AURN

measurements.site_outage_2026_10_22: uk-air.defra.gov.uk returns a 2,038-byte WSP 'Website Temporarily Unavailable' page on every path probed (/data/open-data, /data/automated-monitoring, /data/site-info?site_id=ABD, /), identical for plain and browser user agents; reason given on the page: PHP CVE-2026-109618/109619 security updates
measurements.openaq_probe: OpenAQ v2 API retired (HTTP 410) and v3 requires an API key (HTTP 401), so third-party redistribution of UK AURN data could not be verified anonymously this session and is not claimed
measurements.note: the outage is an infrastructure condition, not a property of the dataset; it is recorded because it blocked reading the licence, not as the reason for the verdict

rejection_reason: Canonical task shape, already declined twice on this bench: day-ahead station-level pollutant concentration/exceedance from the station's own hourly history is the canonical air-quality forecasting task, the same family eccc-hydrometric-daily-flows records as 'the canonical streamflow-forecasting task' (rejected before construction). The bench has been through this family twice already - cpcb-aqi-exceedance (closed) and air4thai-pm25-exceedance (parked, whose next_action states 'a second air-quality task must argue why it is differentiated') - and AURN offers no feature or label that differentiates a third instance: it publishes hourly gas and particulate concentrations at automatic stations, so the only prediction tasks it carries are day-ahead concentration/exceedance forecasting. Adding a UK instance would be a geographic mirror of a declined shape, not a new task. Access/licence note: the publisher site is in a measured maintenance outage (2026-10-22) so its licence was not read; that did not decide this verdict and the door stays closed regardless of what the licence turns out to say.
next_action: None. Re-opened only by a genuinely different task formulation on AURN data (not day-ahead concentration or exceedance forecasting), with the site back online and its licence read from the publisher's own instrument.
